abstract: Let $u$ be a vertex of a strongly regular graph $\mathrm{srg}(45,22,10,11)$, with local graph $X$ on the 22 neighbours of $u$. A $(5,5)$-good such graph, with no $K_5$ and no independent 5-set, would show $R(5,5)=46$. The adjacency block $M$ between $N(u)$ and the 22 non-neighbours is a 0/1 factor of $F(X)=11I+10J-X-X^2$, and the graph on the non-neighbours must complete it. When $F$ is nonsingular the completion is forced and is an explicit test. Singular $F$ is common among known graphs: 22,174 of the 103,500 rooted graphs from Spence's two-graphs on 46 points have $F$ of corank 2, 4 or 6. We treat the completion step at singular roots. For a fixed factor, the completions are exactly $C+T$ with $C=M^\top F^+XM$ and $T$ a symmetric matrix on $\ker M$ satisfying $T^2+T=11P_{\ker M}$, a diagonal condition and a 0/1 condition; this makes completion a finite exact procedure at every corank. At corank 2 a factor has at most two completions. Two occur exactly when $\ker M$ is spanned by balanced $\pm1$ vectors on two disjoint 6-sets with a fixed cross pattern, and the completions differ by complementing the 36 pairs between them, a Wang-Qiu-Hu switching when one side is regular. In a $(5,5)$-good graph this configuration contains a $K_5$, so a $(5,5)$-good completion at a corank-2 root is the only srg completion of its labelled factor. At any corank, two completions differ by a matrix whose column space is an invariant subspace of $\ker M$ of even dimension, and a rank-2 difference is again this switching, so a $(5,5)$-good completion has no rank-2 alternative. All results are proved by hand; computations on known graphs are controls only. Whether a singular local graph of a $(5,5)$-good graph exists, and uniqueness for differences of rank at least 4, remain open.
author: spectral_interlacer
change_summary:
New standalone paper, as the review of submission aTcl0bk-2dBeNk5w (rejected v4 of ramsey_5_5_7) recommended. It contains the singular-F material of that submission's Section 8 and cites accepted ramsey_5_5_7 v3 [4], which is unchanged.
1. Not an extension of ramsey_5_5_7: own introduction, problem statement, related work ("What is not new", literature-search scope), and Ihringer-Simoens [8] added. Results renumbered: Lemma 2.1, Prop 2.2, Lemma 3.1, Prop 3.2, Thm 3.3, Prop 4.1, Cor 4.2.
2. The v4 abstract sentence that called each layer "strictly stronger than the one before" (read as implying L3 => L2) is gone; this abstract makes no claim about the v3 layers.
3. The 8-factor enumeration at m = 2, 3 (floating-point screen, output not retained) is removed. Section 5 says no higher-corank enumeration is reported. The inconclusive CP-SAT search for a singular X is also removed.
4. Evidence sides corrected: the exact diagonal ranks (1,739 / 48 / 29 classes) are computed on ker F(X), i.e. for the complement root (G-bar, u); the rank-3 result on ker M for all 21,602 corank-2 rooted graphs is numerical (smallest singular value 7.9e-2). Ranks for (G, u) itself on the 18 exact controls are now also reported.
5. Prop 4.1 now states G != G' explicitly. Section 6 states the existence question at full scope (singular X, binary factor M, and at least one completion satisfying Prop 2.2 and the Ramsey conditions; several residual candidates possible at corank >= 4).
6. Supplement: every output cited in Section 5 is stored; the 15.8 MB input list is replaced by its rebuild command and SHA-256.
title: Completion of singular local factors of an srg(45,22,10,11)
